US Jobless Claims Stay Low as Productivity Beats Expectations

Initial jobless claims in the United States fell to 199,000 for the week ending August 1, below the 205,000 expected by economists, indicating that the labor market remains resilient. However, continuing jobless claims rose to 1.801 million, exceeding forecasts of 1.789 million, suggesting that while layoffs remain limited, unemployed workers are taking slightly longer to find new jobs.

Separately, unit labor costs increased 1.3% in the second quarter, below expectations of 2.1%, easing concerns about wage-driven inflation. At the same time, nonfarm productivity rose 1.4%, more than double the expected 0.6%, reflecting stronger worker efficiency. The combination of lower labor costs and higher productivity could support the case for moderating inflation while maintaining economic growth.

Financial Performance
- Revenue ₹1,287 Cr (+31% YoY | +18% QoQ).

- EBITDA Margin 10.5% (vs 9.4% YoY | 10.4% QoQ).
- PAT ₹67 Cr (+67% YoY | +20% QoQ).

Operational Highlights
- Revenue growth driven by engineering products.
- Defence shell production contributed.
- Export revenue +53% YoY.
- Exports contributed ~29% of revenue.
- Sales volume 1,22,718 MT (+8.8% YoY).
- Capacity utilisation reached ~98%.
- EBITDA margin improved to 10.8%.
- PAT margin improved to 5.2%.

Concall Highlights
- Received DGQA certification for 155mm M107 Ready-to-Fill artillery shells.
- Secured defence orders worth ₹307.2 Cr.
- Won export order worth USD 13.6 million.
- Export order includes 14,500 MT transmission line structures.
- Defence shell capacity expanding 1.5 lakh → 4 lakh shells/year.
- Strong FY27 growth outlook maintained.
- Growth supported by defence, exports and robust order book.

Management Commentary
- Engineering products driving growth.
- Defence business scaling rapidly.
- Export momentum remains strong.
- Capacity expansion progressing.
- Confident on FY27 growth.
- Robust order book provides visibility.

Key Positives
- Strong revenue growth.
- Robust EBITDA growth.
- PAT surged 67%.
- Margin expansion continued.
- Export business accelerated.
- High capacity utilisation.
- Large defence order wins.
- DGQA certification received.
- Defence capacity expansion underway.

Key Concerns
- Timely defence execution.
- Export demand sustainability.
- Raw material price volatility.
- Capacity expansion execution.

Key Monitorables
- Defence order execution.
- Export order conversion.
- Capacity expansion progress.
- Margin sustainability.
- Engineering product demand.
- Order book growth.

Impact
- Positive.
- Strong operational performance.
- Defence business gaining scale.
- Export momentum improving.
- Growth outlook remains robust.

Key Takeaway
- Goodluck India delivered an impressive Q1 with strong growth across revenue, EBITDA and PAT, supported by engineering products, defence manufacturing and exports. With DGQA certification, a ₹307 crore defence order book, expanding shell capacity and healthy export momentum, the company is well positioned for sustained growth in FY27.

launches include 25 Downtown Tower 5 (Oct/Nov), 25 Estate (Q4), the Thane project 25 Chalet (Q4) and Chembur Phase 2 (luxury, mid and commercial). OCs expected this year span the last tower of Rising City Phase 1 (Ghatkopar), the North and Central towers of 25 South, Bel Air / Tower 1C at Hubtown Premiere (Andheri West), and multiple buildings at Hubtown Polaris (Ahmedabad) and North Star (Mehsana).

**Guidance: FY27 pre-sales of ~INR 6,000 Cr (H2-weighted on launch timing) and collections of ~INR 3,000 Cr. Annuity/commercial income to begin only after ~2.5 years; focus stays on the MMR region, with new projects pursued on an asset-light/partnership basis.**

**Outlook:** Hubtown is positioning around three levers, monetising a premium Mumbai-centric portfolio, consolidating marquee assets via Hubtown 2.0, and de-leveraging towards a net-debt-free balance sheet. Reported earnings will stay lumpy under project-completion accounting, and historically sub-10% ROE should improve as refinancing lowers the interest burden, price rises stick and deliveries pick up through H2. At CMP, the stock trades at ~1.2x P/B (book value ~INR 184), a modest multiple against a ~INR 11,583 Cr contracted pipeline yet to be recognised and combined post-merger GDV pegged at over INR 1 lakh Cr, though realisation of that embedded value hinges on NCLT approvals, execution and OC timelines.

**Hubtown Q1 Concall Snippets

Hubtown 2.0 Unlocks A New Growth Chapter**
Q1 FY27 marks the beginning of an inflection year for **Hubtown Limited (BSE: 532799; NSE: HUBTOWN; Market Cap: ~INR 2,660 Cr)**. Pre-sales of ₹535 Cr, up 8% year on year, demonstrate continued pricing power across their premium and ultra-luxury portfolio. This performance is anchored in a land moat that took 35 years to build. With ₹11,583 Cr of contracted balance revenue and three merger schemes progressing, FY27 is the year Hubtown's investment thesis begins to manifest in reported numbers.

**The Embedded Pipeline: Value Yet To Be Recognised**

The least understood part of the story is the embedded book. Across ongoing developments (including the to-be-merged entities), Hubtown has cumulative pre-sales of ~INR 14,835 Cr, of which ~INR 8,352 Cr is already collected and only ~INR 3,252 Cr recognised as revenue so far. That leaves ~INR 11,583 Cr of contracted pipeline still to flow through the P&L as projects complete and hand over, much of it already collected and simply awaiting the final milestone. Beyond this, Hubtown carries ~34 msf of planned development across 25 Chalet, 25 Estate, Season Phase 2, Sunstream City, Hubtown Commercial and Rising City, a multi-year growth runway to layer on top of a ~13 msf delivery track record built over three decades. The company was also the No. 2 top-selling residential developer in South Mumbai during the quarter.

**Hubtown 2.0: Consolidating The Marquee Assets**

The transformative piece is Hubtown 2.0, the amalgamation that consolidates the marquee luxury projects (25 Downtown, 25 West and 25 South, effective 1 April 2025, subject to approvals) into the listed entity. The first two schemes have received key approvals and await final NCLT sanction, while the third is progressing through the regulatory process.

__Absorbing 4 promoter-group entities via NCLT to unify assets and eliminate cross-holdings.__

**Saicharan Consultancy:** Merging to boost Hubtown’s revenue share by 21.17% in the Ghatkopar Rising City project.

**25 West Realty:** Merging the luxury Bandra West asset to unlock a lifetime revenue potential of ₹6,000 crore.

**25 South:** Absorbing the 25 South Premium project with a Total Carpet area of 0.96 msf

**25 Downtown:** Large scale project in South Mumbai, in terms of revenue and area under development and total development of ~3.68 msf.

On completion, the ongoing development portfolio expands from ~7.13 msf to over 34 msf, backed by ~347 acres of landholding, with combined GDV expected to exceed INR 1 lakh Cr over time. Post-merger promoter holding moves to the ~68-70% range, as the schemes are issued against equity.

**Deleveraging And Refinancing In Motion**

Total borrowings have been cut to ~INR 5,181 Cr, of which INR 3,950 Cr sits in the to-be-merged companies and is project-linked and self-liquidating, funded directly by project cash flows. Legacy bank, NBFC and foreign-fund debt has been fully retired, and the company targets a net-debt-free balance sheet by FY2031. Management noted refinancing options improved sharply over the last quarter and it is looking to refinance ~INR 2,800 Cr of high-cost debt currently carrying 14-20% rates, with substantial savings expected once term sheets are finalised. All project surpluses remain ring-fenced towards debt repayment before any redeployment. On the capital side, enabling resolutions are in place for a preferential issue, QIP and FCCB (~INR 1,400 Cr / USD 150 Mn), with management preferring a single tranche once markets improve. Two promoter pledges remain outstanding, with release targeted within FY27.

**Pricing And Demand Hold Firm At The Top End**

Luxury demand and walk-ins stayed strong through a seasonally soft Q1, while mid-segment walk-ins were muted but conversion remained healthy. The higher floors (51st to 85th) of 25 Downtown will open strategically from October at premium pricing, with the typical higher-versus-lower floor gap running 30-40%, while 25 West has already risen INR 30,000-40,000/sq ft over ~1.5 years.

**Sedemac Mechatronics - R&D-led growth story
**
Sedemac’s journey started with sensor-less commutation (SLC) - its key technology moat that helped it scale rapidly in 2W/3W starter generators. Now, the same R&D engine is being leveraged to build the next layers of growth.

1. Core business still has runway: ISG penetration could rise from 40-45% → 55-60%, while Sedemac’s market share could expand from 36-38% → 46-48% by FY29.

2. EVs become the next growth engine: Its e2W/e3W motor controllers are expected to grow at a massive ~75% CAGR, potentially reaching 10-12% market share by FY29.

3. New growth layers are getting added: Sedemac is entering power tools, LCVs, CV after-treatment & EFI systems, while its genset business (~75% market share) continues to scale.

4. Capacity is being built ahead of demand: With existing plants at >90% utilisation, two new facilities should triple capacity, while Chennai land provides further expansion optionality.

HSBC expects FY26-29 Revenue / EBITDA / PAT CAGR of ~32% / 35% / 49%, with ROCE improving to ~29%.

The backbone remains R&D (~7% of revenue) allowing Sedemac to repeatedly build new products around its core technology.
